_comment: In-country crop calendar per growing origin, used by the WEATHER panel to label phenological stage (flowering / sizing / harvest) so a rainfall number reads as a reason to care. These are NOT arrival windows — for when fruit reaches the US market (~3-5 weeks after harvest for ocean freight) see seasons.json. Two files, two concepts: seasons.json = US arrivals; crop_calendar.json = in-country phenology. Dates are MM-DD and may wrap the new year. A window may carry an optional 'label' (e.g. a named bloom); where several labelled windows of the same stage match a date, current_stage() returns the stage plus all matching labels. Single name for the bloom stage: 'flowering' (Michoacán's four blooms are flowering windows with labels). 'applies_to' shares a calendar with sibling regions AND with the differently-keyed ENSO/weather aliases (weather regions are keyed 'michoacan'/'jalisco'/'ventura'/'san_diego'; the ENSO origin is 'mx_michoacan').

origins._note: Four overlapping blooms, each harvested ~12-15 months after bloom. Both bloom and harvest windows union to all twelve months, so Michoacán never has an off-window and 'stage' alone is uninformative — the bloom label carries the signal. Jalisco follows the same cycle and is important as Flor Loca supplement when Michoacán dips. Bloom stored under 'flowering' for one consistent stage name.
Bloom window is inferred from the standard coastal California cycle, not supplied — verify.
